A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same federated mixture-of-experts work, renamed from Fed-ZERO to FedJETs. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR10/CIFAR100 experiments, including personalization results, expert-initialization ablations, and client-sampling analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, incremental-learning experiments, matched-expert controls, and clustering analysis.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the frozen common expert, learned gating network, top-K selection, anchor-client losses, aggregation, and per-sample expert selection during inference. The rename and revised partition descriptions do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR10/CIFAR100, but v2 extends Dirichlet evaluation to CIFAR100 and adds incremental-learning scenarios with growing and successively replaced client pools (Appendices B.2 and E). These expand coverage from static populations to changing training distributions and label availability.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated FedProx and SCAFFOLD comparisons, including unsuccessful SCAFFOLD outcomes, and introduces FedSR/FedADG comparisons in Appendix G. Average Ensembles is removed from the Dirichlet comparison in Table 3, although retained elsewhere. The evaluated comparator set therefore expands substantially.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix A reports sample allocation with replacement where v1 described allocation without replacement. Table 3 changes from accuracy after 2,500 iterations to best accuracy over the last ten evaluations. Added protocols include 200/600-round client-group schedules and M = K controls at two and five experts. These establish reported protocol changes, not proof that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Existing common-expert, initialization, anchor-ratio, and per-sample analyses are retained or relocated. v2 adds adaptation/retention tests under client turnover, matched-expert-count controls against FedMix, and a K-means client-clustering case study (Appendices E, F, and H), substantially broadening robustness and diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Shaded bands in v1 Figure 3 disappear from the corresponding v2 Figure 7, while other plots retain bands. Neither PDF defines their statistical meaning or computation, and ensemble seed information is unchanged. Whether this changes uncertainty reporting or only plot styling remains unresolved.

E6.justification: Retained Table 1 entries and Tables 2 and 4 are unchanged. Table 3 replaces CIFAR10 scores, including 80.03% becoming 80.8% for the proposed method, and adds CIFAR100 results, including 77.8%, under revised reported protocols. New baseline, matched-expert, domain-generalization, and incremental results substantially expand the findings; the switching-client experiment reports FedJETs about two percentage points below FedAvg.

T1.justification: The FL objective, routing definitions, and normal/anchor-client losses retain the same mathematics. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added. v2's suggestion of future theoretical investigation is not a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The central personalization, specialization, and communication claims remain. The introduction narrows the headline CIFAR10 advantage by changing the second-best score from approximately 58% to 71%, while retaining approximately 95% for the proposed method. The conclusion still retains the older 58% comparison.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of baseline instability, anchor regularization under client turnover, limitations of domain-generalization methods with many clients, and the claimed inadequacy of clustering mixed client distributions. It also softens the existing assertion that a phase transition exists into a tentative interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies four labels per ordinary CIFAR10 client, details Dirichlet anchor construction, and documents initialization choices for added baselines. Core optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, and local-epoch details are retained. These are limited documentation additions alongside the separately identified protocol revisions.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning beyond v1's ensemble/FedMix discussion to federated domain generalization and explicitly argues against client clustering for mixed distributions. It also strengthens the novelty positioning around meaningful expert specialization. FedSR/FedADG and related studies are newly cited; SCAFFOLD and FedProx were already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The method is renamed and zero-shot terminology becomes just-in-time. v2 edits explanatory paragraphs, separates overview from system details, and moves end-to-end and distribution-based discussions into organized appendices. Most introductory and mathematical exposition remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redraws Figure 1, revises plot legends and displays, relocates comparison plots, and expands Table 3. It removes v1's conceptual anchor diagram and benchmarking Table 5, while adding distribution, incremental-learning, and clustering figures and new comparison tables. Typography and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: The matched-expert controls in Appendix F address v1's confounding between method and total expert capacity, while additional baselines and client-turnover tests better delimit performance. These strengthen empirical support, but the gain is tempered by unreconciled sampling/result-selection descriptions and the conclusion's stale 58% comparison.
